headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can feed transformers’ shell/file/browser pipeline with sensitive content by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through MCP-compatible/API surfaces, while transformers can read files, run browsers, and execute shell commands. If firecrawl output is copied into transformers’ prompts or files, hostile page content can steer downstream tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is passed into transformers as trusted text or files, prompt injection is plausible.
IF transformers is allowed to act on browser-scraped content without provenance checks, hostile instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any firecrawl output enters transformers.
Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward.
Use a separate workspace for firecrawl outputs and transformers inputs.
Disable browser automation on untrusted pages for the first run.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, and transformers has read/write filesystem plus broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive inputs from firecrawl can be read and retransmitted by transformers, creating an exfiltration path. Because both profiles expose broad egress and file access, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF firecrawl stores scraped content or API keys in a shared directory, transformers can read them.
IF transformers sends its context or loaded files to external services, leaked data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep firecrawl secrets in a separate secret store.
Use distinct, non-overlapping directories for each agent.
Rotate any API keys used by firecrawl before pairing.
Review transformers logs for file contents and redact them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and API/MCP-style access, while transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both operate on the same project tree, they can overwrite each other’s artifacts or model files. The overlap is real but not inherently destructive, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF transformers installs packages in the same environment firecrawl uses, dependency drift can break runs.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run one agent at a time when modifying shared artifacts.
Pin package versions before any transformers install step.
Use read-only mounts for firecrawl outputs.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and transformers can run browsers and shell commands that may act on that output. If transformers treats firecrawl results as authoritative without verification, a bad scrape can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. The pathway exists in default-style pipelines, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF transformers consumes firecrawl output without validation, errors can propagate into later steps.
IF downstream scripts use scraped facts to make decisions, a bad scrape can trigger incorrect actions.
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action uses scraped data.
Require source URLs alongside extracted facts.
Sample-check a few outputs against the original page.
Log transformations from scrape to action.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for firecrawl outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl handles API keys and web content, while transformers can persist files and send data over broad network egress. If regulated or personal data is scraped and then written or transmitted by transformers, retention and residency controls may diverge. No residency or certification data is provided, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is scraped by firecrawl and stored by transformers, retention policy mismatch is possible.
IF transformers transmits stored outputs to external endpoints, residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Classify data before passing it between agents.
Avoid scraping regulated data unless retention is defined.
Delete intermediate files after each run.
Confirm where transformers writes logs and artifacts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
